root_motivation: Who: the operator of prod mcphost, and every reader of the tenant table (the funnel, the PMF count, `admin.tenants`). What: synthetic tenants minted by implicit signup accumulate forever. Why they cannot fix it: the host offers no lifecycle for a tenant row. The only disable paths are a tenant's own `host.self_offboard` (`src/db.rs:6740-6748`, needs the tenant's credential) and `admin.tenant_disable` (`src/db.rs:6703-6716`, a hand action on prod data). The harness never captured the credential (`onboarding.url` is the only one returned, `src/handler.rs:8141-8150`), and an admin sweep of prod rows needs Joe's word each time. Cost: 177 dead rows per full chain run, 2,990 live synthetic tenants on 10-22, every one counted by any query that forgets to filter `synthetic`, and a tenant table whose growth is driven by the test harness rather than by users.
user_persona: An agent that calls host.sync.create with a source ref and gets a scheduled mirror in one call; Operator Joe who reads docs/tools.md and llms.txt and knows both were rendered from the SourceKind enum.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given subject fixture A (both synthetic markers, implicit, unclaimed, unpaid, after the floor, idle 2 days) and seven variants: claimed, origin external, idle 1 hour, paid, `synthetic` NULL, billing_ref set, before the floor, When `prune_once` runs with the default window, Then only A ends `disabled = 1, disabled_reason = 'idle_expired'`, its session released, every kind's `on_tenant_removed` run; the variants are unchanged.

Given the env var unset, set to `3`, and set to `0`, When the policy table is seeded at start twice and `prune_once` runs on fixture A (idle 2 days), Then the stored window is 1, 3 and 0 days, `floor_unix` is set by the first seed and unchanged by the second, A is expired only in the unset case, and `retention_policy` lists `synthetic_implicit_tenants` beside the existing rows.

Given an expired tenant, When a call arrives on its `/u/{url_secret}/mcp` URL and another with its key as `tenant_key`, Then both are refused with the error a self-offboarded tenant gets and the reason field reads `idle_expired`, while a keyless call from a different peer still mints a new tenant, so expiry never blocks the front door.

Given `mcphost contract dump` in a clean checkout and a server of that build, When both are read, Then `contracts/host-tools.v1.json` carries a top-level `tenant_lifecycle` (selector, env var, default, reason) built by `api_contract` from the policy constants, `contract_version` follows the file's rule, `GET /contract.json` returns the binary's bytes, and `contract --check` fails when a test-only override moves the default.

Given 6,000 subjects and 10 non-subjects, When `prune_once` runs twice concurrently and once more on an empty set, Then every subject is expired exactly once over more than one batch, a subject touched by `touch_last_seen` between batches is skipped, non-subjects are unchanged, each run writes one `prune_log` row with `expired`, `skipped_billing`, `would_expire` (0 and no error for the empty run), and no teardown ran twice.

Given `host.doctor` called by a subject tenant, a claimed tenant, an external tenant, and the subject again with the window set to 0, When each reads the response, Then `tenant_lifecycle` is `{subject: true, idle_days, expires_at_unix}` with `expires_at_unix` equal to the call's `now + window` for the subject, and `{subject: false, expires_at_unix: null}` for the other three, computed from the `CLASS` and `FLOOR` terms.

Given one tenant expired by the sweep, one self-offboarded, and 3 backlog rows older than the floor, When `admin.tenants` runs filtered by `disabled_reason: "idle_expired"` then unfiltered, and `admin.funnel` is read, Then the filter returns only the expired one, every unfiltered row carries `expires_at_unix` (null for a non-subject), `tenants_idle_expired` is a `COUNT` of 1 after a restart, and the latest `would_expire` is 3.

Given prod after this change deploys, When the contract is fetched anonymously, Then `tenant_lifecycle.disabled_reason` reads `idle_expired` and the selector names `origin` `synthetic` (Live; evidence: `curl -sS https://mcphost.dev/contract.json | jq -e '.tenant_lifecycle.disabled_reason == "idle_expired" and .tenant_lifecycle.selector.origin == "synthetic" and .tenant_lifecycle.selector.signup_source == "implicit"'`)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: Live (prod; evidence: curl -sS https://mcphost.dev/contract.json | jq -e '.tenant_lifecycle.disabled_reason == "idle_expired"')

scope: src/sync/mod.rs: the SourceKind registry, host.sync.create/list/get/delete/run_now, and the trigger tick's sync pass writing a not_implemented sync_runs receipt.
migrations/0130_syncs.sql: syncs and sync_runs tables; Plan.syncs_max (free 5, pro 50) and the quota_syncs_max, connection_missing and schedule_too_frequent error codes.
www/llms.txt gains a generated Data sync section and docs/tools.md the source.kind enum, both rendered from SourceKind.
non_goals: Fetching rows (the pull PRD); push or conflict handling (the two-way PRD); type inference beyond text columns; any new OAuth flow.

additional.main_database_tables: syncs and sync_runs live in the main database (migration 0130), not a per-tenant file, so the tick's sync pass is one indexed query across tenants.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can an agent not keep a host table equal to a sheet?
five_whys_trace.a: No verb registers an external source; the agent would own a puller, a token and a diff loop.
host.table.append cannot update a row and host.trigger.set only calls a published tool.
One SourceKind enum generates the schema, docs and dispatch, so the five kinds cannot drift.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What is source.secret?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The NAME of a host.secret (stored as secret_name), never a value, so no secret-named field exists on a Debug struct.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Do push and two_way modes run?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: They are accepted at create with status pending_mode (the PRD default) and the tick skips them.
